title: Frozen Standard10 plus native-v6 zero-residual feasibility
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A dual-contract learned policy can preserve Standard10 legacy-v4 logits exactly at initialization while exposing native physical-v6 observations only to a separate trainable residual, avoiding the observation-contract destruction seen in direct rebound PPO.
material_change: Implement a default-off wrapper with a frozen legacy-v4 base actor/value and a zero-initialized native-v6 residual actor/value. Test exact parity on 4,096 reachable states, legal-mask invariance, gradient isolation, deterministic checkpoint roundtrip, and post-update sensitivity. No poker-strength training or Slumbot calls.
baseline: Standard10 bridge fresh20k -24.5683 bb/100; shallow existing-network PPO fresh5k -64.2932; direct native-v6 rebound and longer PPO variants were materially worse.
notes: Admission requires bitwise-equal base/wrapper logits and values at zero residual on every state, identical legal greedy slot, zero base gradients, nonzero residual gradients, and exact roundtrip outputs. This is only an architecture gate.

result.summary: A frozen Standard10 legacy-v4 base plus zero-initialized native-v6 residual was exercised on 4,096 reachable states from 953 trajectories. Logits, values, and legal greedy choices exactly matched the base at initialization; gradients and updates were isolated to the residual; serialized outputs round-tripped exactly. Full alpha_holdem suite passed 224 tests.
result.conclusion: The architecture removes the immediate observation-contract regression while exposing native-v6 information to trainable weights. This proves mechanism and preservation only; the post-update residual checkpoint is a gradient probe, not a poker candidate.
result.next_step: Implement a small matched reward-training smoke with the base permanently frozen, zero residual initialization, common training seeds, tightly bounded residual logits, and untouched common-deck evaluation. Do not allocate Slumbot until a separately seeded treatment beats its zero-residual control broadly.
